column3: Decision graph CLI for tracing how software decisions evolve
column4:
A Rust CLI tool that builds a directed graph of your software decisions as you make them.
Every goal, action, decision, and outcome gets logged in real-time and linked together.
Includes a web viewer, git commit linking, branch-based grouping, and multi-user sync via patches.
Ships via Homebrew tap.

column3: Neural network loss function explorer
column4: An interactive tool for exploring and comparing neural network loss functions.\nVisualizes how different loss functions behave across parameter spaces.

column3: Jam analytics dashboard for Phish 3.0 era
column4: A comprehensive analytics dashboard for Phish jam data. Filter by year and song,\nsee batting averages for jams, duration timelines, jamchart rates, and flip through\ndetailed cards for every notable performance. Built as a Phoenix LiveView with D3 charts.

column3: 4-bit quantization, safetensors, and Bumblebee + EMLX for Apple Silicon
column4:
A series of libraries and experiments to run large language models locally on a MacBook Pro.
Includes a safetensors parser for Elixir, 4-bit quantization support for Bumblebee,
and EMLX bindings to leverage Apple's MLX framework from Elixir. The goal: run inference
on Apple Silicon without leaving the BEAM.

column3: TV writer overlap explorer
column4: Explore which TV writers have worked together across different shows.\nDiscover unexpected connections in the television writing world.

column3: An ORM written in Temper
column4: A from-scratch ORM built in the Temper programming language. Explores what database\nabstractions look like in a language with a novel type system. Handles schema definition,\nquery building, and migrations.

column3: A bot that posts like me, in Python
column4: A Python bot trained on my writing style that generates and posts content that sounds like me.\nUses fine-tuned language model adapters to capture voice and topic preferences.

column3: Porting the posting bot to Elixir using local LLM work
column4: An Elixir version of the Bobby Posts bot, leveraging the Bumblebee quantization\nand EMLX work to run inference on the BEAM. Proves the full local-LLM-in-Elixir\npipeline works end-to-end.

column3: A local LLM running on my iPhone, coming to the App Store for free
column4: An iPhone app that runs language model inference entirely on-device using Apple's MLX framework.\nA truly portable, offline-capable AI assistant in your pocket. Built in Swift with a clean native UI.\nWill be released for free on the App Store.

column3: A modern GenStage tutorial for the Elixir ecosystem
column4: An updated, comprehensive tutorial on Elixir's GenStage for building\ndata processing pipelines. Covers producers, consumers, back-pressure,\nand real-world patterns with modern Elixir.

column3: A blog post that became its own LiveView application
column4: What started as a blog post about the surprisingly deep history of tree law\ngrew into a full interactive LiveView application. Covers centuries of legal\nprecedent around trees, property rights, and neighbor disputes.

column3: Found a bug in the Temper compiler and built a demo repo
column4: While working with the Temper programming language, I discovered a bug in its\nRust backend. Built a minimal reproduction repository and documented the issue.

column3: Experiments porting Phoenix HEEx templates to Rust, Lua, C#, Java, Python, and JS
column4: A series of experiments using Temper to port Phoenix's HEEx template engine to\nsix other programming languages. Explores what Phoenix-style server-rendered\ntemplates look like outside the Elixir ecosystem.

column3: A complete software suite for thermal receipt printers
column4: Software for driving thermal receipt printers for creative and practical uses.\nIncludes drivers, formatting libraries, and integration with various input sources.\nPowers the photo booth, remote printing, and direct message receipt features.

column3: Live-stream blog drafts from Zed to Phoenix via a custom LSP
column4: A Language Server Protocol implementation that streams your blog drafts in real-time\nfrom the Zed editor to a Phoenix LiveView. Includes a Zed extension and a Phoenix\nAPI endpoint. Readers can watch you write.

column3: A personal todo app
column4: A personal todo application built for my own workflow.

column3: A real over-the-air TV channel from magnetic media archives
column4: Software that turns a collection of digitized magnetic media (VHS tapes, etc.) into\nan actual broadcast TV channel in our house. Integrates with the archive to schedule\nand transmit content over the air using a software-defined radio.

column3: Demonstrations of decision archaeology on React and stacked git workflows
column4: Showcases of using Deciduous to retroactively trace decision histories in existing\ncodebases. Includes demos on a React project and a stacked-git workflow, showing\nhow to reconstruct the reasoning behind past architectural choices.

column3: Various apps that vacuum up and process the Bluesky firehose
column4: A collection of applications that consume the Bluesky/AT Protocol firehose\nfor different purposes: link curation, content filtering, community discovery,\nand real-time feed processing.

column3: A portable photo booth that prints on receipt paper
column4: A portable photo booth project that captures photos and prints them as strips\non a thermal receipt printer. Combines hardware tinkering with creative software\nto make a fun party/event fixture.

column2: Send Me a Photo From Your Day
column3: A social project where friends send photos that print on my receipt printer
column4: A social experiment where friends can send me a photo from their day and it prints\ndirectly on my receipt printer at home. Grew out of the photo booth and receipt printer\nsoftware suite. A physical, tangible way to stay connected.

column3: A Nathan For You social network with video search and GIF creation
column4: A social network dedicated entirely to Nathan For You content. Features video search\nby caption file, GIF creation from show clips, and community features. Was accidentally\nuseful as a general-purpose video search and GIF tool.

column3: An MCP server that roasts you based on your browser history
column4: A Model Context Protocol server that reads your browser history and generates\nroasts about your browsing habits. Includes a screenshot judgement mode and\na dedicated roasting interface.

column3: The original GenStage tutorial
column4: The original GenStage tutorial that kicked off a series of Elixir data pipeline\nexplorations. Covers the fundamentals of producers, consumers, and back-pressure.

column3: Interactive census and PLUTO data visualization for New York City
column4: Draw on a map of New York City and get instant population estimates for the area.\nCombines 2020 Census data with NYC PLUTO tax lot data. Features a toggleable\npopulation density heatmap overlay.

column3: Extract GIFs from concert videos with a retro Mac interface
column4: A web tool that extracts segments from YouTube concert videos and converts them\nto high-quality GIFs using a two-pass FFmpeg pipeline. Features frame selection,\noverlay text, math CAPTCHA verification, and a retro Mac OS interface.

column3: Interactive map of 418+ Bluesky communities with 545K+ people
column4: A D3/Canvas visualization mapping the community structure of Bluesky.\nDiscovered via graph analysis of the social network. Browse 418+ communities,\nsee how they connect, and find your place in the network.

column3: Real-time firehose visualizations: emoji streams, jetstream comparisons, and more
column4: A collection of real-time visualizations built on the Bluesky AT Protocol firehose.\nWatch emoji usage across the network, compare different firehose relay performance,\nand browse YouTube videos shared on Bluesky.

column3: A live code mirror experiment
column4: An interactive code mirror that reflects and transforms input in real-time.

column3: Upload photos and arrange them into grid collages
column4: A web tool for creating photo collages. Upload 2-36 images, configure the grid\nlayout, randomize arrangement, and download a full-resolution collage. Features\nmath CAPTCHA and rate limiting.

column3: Real-time MTA bus and train tracking on an interactive map
column4: Live tracking of MTA buses and trains on interactive Leaflet maps.\nSee real-time vehicle positions, route lines, and stop information\nfor New York City's transit system.

column3: Generative art engine written in Temper, compiled to JavaScript
column4: A generative art engine written in Temper — a memory-safe language that compiles to JS, Python, Java, C#, Lua, and Rust. The engine runs three algorithms (Bauhaus grid, flow-field particles, Mondrian subdivision) driven by a splitmix32 PRNG, so every seed produces the same piece deterministically on any backend. In the browser it renders to Canvas with a history navigator and PNG export.
